newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil closes higher, crude recovers.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil closes higher, crude recovers.

text.p: IPE Oct gas oil closed $4.25 a tonne higher after range-trading most of the day, inspiring Brent crude to test the highs after dipping earlier on weaker NYMEX heating oil, brokers said.
Oct gas oil closed at $218.25 a tonne after breaking through $216.50 a tonne. A futures broker said gas oil was expected to hold in the $215.50-$218.50 range.

"Our preference is for the long side with a selling extreme above $218.50. We would be sceptical about buying too close to that level. A break of $219.50 would see us joining the market on the long side," the broker said.

Traders said NYMEX heating oil failed to provide much direction with trading thin due to the Jewish Yom Kippur holiday. The weakness of gasoline has also continued to pull down the NYMEX oil complex, they added.
"Gasoline is the unpopular product at the moment. The retracement was on the back of product weakness and there were not enough traders in the market," the broker said.
Nov Brent initially moved down shortly after the NYMEX open after starting the week stronger on concerns over the health of Russian President Boris Yeltsin.
Nov Brent dipped to an intra-day low of $21.83 a barrel before recovering to $22.07 a barrel, up eight cents.
"While heating oil was providing strength on Friday and overnight and crude was a reluctant player, now that heat is coming off crude is coming down to more comfortable levels," a floor trader said.
He added Monday's levels were likely to set the tone for the rest of the week now that Gulf tensions had eased and the Iraq factor was no longer contributing to price volatility.
